Ritu Project — Carboplatin Cohort (Local/Early)

Author

Tianqi Ouyang

Published

April 9, 2026

Ritu cohort — Local/Early stage only. This page repeats the Jiaxuan carboplatin analysis on the subset of patients with tumor_stage == "Local/Early", leaving N = 189 carboplatin patients. tumor_stage is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set because it is constant within this cohort. Everything else is unchanged.

Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page. AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 5, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in Data Management and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. Read both models with their event counts in view — 23 AKI and 11 CKD-composite events in 189 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See RITU_PROJECT.md.

1 Setup

Code 
# Force UTF-8 locale so kable captions and other strings render real Unicode
# (e.g. em-dash) instead of <U+2014> escape sequences.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8"))

# Output directory for downloadable Word tables (placed under docs/ so the
# rendered website can serve them from ../tables/carbo/<name>.docx).
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/carbo"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Output directory for editable PowerPoint copies of every figure. A knitr
# plot hook (defined below) saves last_plot() to docs/pptx/carbo/<label>.pptx
# and appends a download link after the figure in the rendered HTML.
dir.create("docs/pptx/carbo", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/pptx/carbo", mustWork = TRUE)
pptx_rel_prefix <- "../pptx/carbo/"

.pptx_written <- new.env()
.pptx_pair    <- new.env()
.docx_written <- new.env()

# Relative path for Word-table download links from rendered docs/qmd/*.html
docx_rel_prefix <- paste0("../", sub("^docs/", "", docx_dir), "/")

# Save a plain data frame to Word and register it, so the chunk hook below can
# put a download link under the table. Named after the chunk label, as the
# PPTX files are; a chunk holding two tables passes a suffix for the second.
.tbl_docx <- function(x, suffix = NULL) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(invisible(x))
  name <- if (is.null(suffix)) label else paste0(label, "_", suffix)
  ok <- tryCatch({
    flextable::flextable(as.data.frame(x)) |>
      flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
      flextable::autofit() |>
      flextable::save_as_docx(path = file.path(docx_dir, paste0(name, ".docx")))
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) {
    txt <- if (is.null(suffix)) "Download Word table"
           else paste0("Download Word table (", suffix, ")")
    .docx_written[[label]] <- c(.docx_written[[label]],
      stats::setNames(paste0(docx_rel_prefix, name, ".docx"), txt))
  }
  invisible(x)
}

.save_pptx <- function(p, path) {
  tryCatch({
    doc <- officer::read_pptx()
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content",
                              master = "Office Theme")
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
                            location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body"))
    print(doc, target = path)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(filename) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(filename)
  pair <- .pptx_pair[[label]]
  if (!is.null(pair) && inherits(pair$default, "ggplot") && inherits(pair$fine, "ggplot")) {
    p1 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
    p2 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    ok1 <- .save_pptx(pair$default, p1)
    ok2 <- .save_pptx(pair$fine,    p2)
    rels <- c(if (ok1) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx"),
              if (ok2) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    if (length(rels)) .pptx_written[[label]] <- rels
    return(filename)
  }
  p <- tryCatch(ggplot2::last_plot(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(filename)
  pptx_path <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
  if (.save_pptx(p, pptx_path)) {
    .pptx_written[[label]] <- paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx")
  }
  filename
})

local({
  default_chunk_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
    out <- default_chunk_hook(x, options)
    label <- options$label
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.pptx_written[[label]])) {
      rel <- .pptx_written[[label]]
      if (length(rel) == 2) {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download top plot as PowerPoint</a> · <a href="%s" download>📊 Download bottom (10 %% ticks)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1], rel[2])
      } else {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download as PowerPoint (editable)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1])
      }
      out <- paste0(out, link)
    }
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.docx_written[[label]])) {
      v <- .docx_written[[label]]
      out <- paste0(out, paste(sprintf(
        '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📄 %s</a></p>\n\n',
        v, names(v)), collapse = ""))
    }
    out
  })
})

# --- Sparse-outcome guard (Ritu cohort) --------------------------------------
# Restricting to Local/Early disease leaves several outcomes with very few
# events (90-day death = 2; thrombocytopenia grade 3 and the individual
# hospitalization reasons are in the single digits). A model that cannot be
# estimated raises an error, which would abort the entire render, so every
# table / row / figure helper is wrapped below. On success the output is exactly
# what the Jiaxuan version produces; on failure a short note is emitted in place
# of the table or figure. No model specification is changed.
.wrap_tbl <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-warning}\n",
    "## Model not estimable in this cohort\n\n",
    "Too few events among the ", nrow(dat), " Local/Early patients to fit ",
    "this model with the full adjuster set.\n\n",
    "Error: `", conditionMessage(e), "`\n:::\n")))
}
.wrap_row <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(time_var, status_var, label, ...) tryCatch(
    f(time_var, status_var, label, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      ev <- tryCatch(
        sum(as.character(dat[[status_var]]) == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e2) NA_integer_)
      tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = label, Model = "not estimable",
        N = NA_integer_, `Excluded (missing cov.)` = NA_integer_,
        Events = as.integer(ev),
        `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = "not estimable", `p-value` = "\u2014")
    })
}
.wrap_plot <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e)
    ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.3,
        label = paste0("Model not estimable in this cohort\n",
                       "(too few events among the ", nrow(dat),
                       " Local/Early patients)\n\n",
                       strwrap(conditionMessage(e), width = 60,
                               prefix = "\n", initial = ""))) +
      ggplot2::theme_void())
}

# Table 1 via tableone. Factor-like columns (factor / character / logical and
# indicator columns of 0/1) are summarised as n (%); every other numeric column
# as median [IQR], except the variables named in `normal_vars` (mean (SD)).
# Categorical variables with any observed cell < 5 get Fisher's exact test.
tableone_mat <- function(d, strata = NULL, normal_vars = "age") {
  d     <- as.data.frame(d)
  vars  <- setdiff(names(d), strata)
  is_fl <- vapply(d[vars], function(x)
    is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) ||
      (is.numeric(x) && all(stats::na.omit(unique(x)) %in% c(0, 1))),
    logical(1))
  fct_vars  <- vars[is_fl]
  cont_vars <- vars[!is_fl]

  if (is.null(strata)) {
    tab   <- tableone::CreateTableOne(vars = vars, data = d,
                                      factorVars = fct_vars, test = FALSE)
    small <- NULL
  } else {
    tab <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = vars, strata = strata, data = d, factorVars = fct_vars,
      addOverall = TRUE, test = TRUE, argsExact = list(workspace = 2 * 10^7))
    small <- fct_vars[vapply(fct_vars, function(v)
      any(table(d[[v]], d[[strata]]) < 5), logical(1))]
    if (!length(small)) small <- NULL
  }

  mat <- print(tab, nonnormal = setdiff(cont_vars, normal_vars), exact = small,
               showAllLevels = TRUE, missing = TRUE, printToggle = FALSE,
               noSpaces = TRUE, quote = FALSE)
  tibble::as_tibble(cbind(Characteristic = rownames(mat), mat),
                    .name_repair = "unique")
}

save_tbl_docx <- function(tbl, docx_name) {
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(tbl)
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir,
                                               paste0(docx_name, ".docx")))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Load the Local/Early cohort, then keep only carboplatin patients
dat <- readRDS("ritu_final_master.rds") %>%
  filter(platin_group == "Carboplatin") %>%
  # Ritu: clear factor levels left empty by the cohort filter above,
  # so the model matrices stay full rank (cmp_status_* excluded --
  # their 0/1/2 coding is relied on downstream).
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

# Create eGFR ratio: CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (unindexed) / Cockcroft-Gault
# Also create per-10 mL/min rescaled versions of cockcroft and CKD-EPI for
# reporting (HRs per 1 mL/min are clinically uninterpretable; convention in
# nephro-onc is per 10 mL/min — bio_agent confirmed). Adjusters keep raw scale.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # Capped versions (for dose discrepancy calculations)
    cockcroft_cap125 = pmin(cockcroft, 125),
    # ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex_cap125 already exists in data
    # Ratio uses UNCAPPED eGFR
    egfr_ratio    = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / cockcroft,
    egfr_ratio_per10 = -egfr_ratio * 10,  # per 0.1-unit *decrease* reporting scale
    egfr_discrepancy = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft,
    # per-10-mL/min DECLINE reporting scale for eGFR discrepancy: HR for this
    # variable reads as the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower
    # discrepancy (i.e., when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 10 mL/min farther below CG).
    egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10,
    # Sensitivity-analysis eGFR ratio (Section 16):
    # numerator = CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C only (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed)
    # denominator = CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine only (baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed)
    # per10 below is the per-0.1 DECLINE reporting scale.
    egfr_ratio_sens       = baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_ratio_sens_per10 = -egfr_ratio_sens * 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR (new primary exposure):
    # egfr_diff_pct = 100 * (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed - Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault
    # egfr_diff_pct_per10: HR reads as multiplicative change per 10 percentage-point DECLINE.
    egfr_diff_pct         = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    egfr_diff_pct_per10   = -egfr_diff_pct / 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR for sensitivity analysis:
    # numerator - denominator = CKD-EPI 2012 CysC - CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, both unindexed.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens        = 100 * (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed - baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed) / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10  = -egfr_diff_pct_sens / 10,
    # Binary form of the same exposure: 1 when the cystatin C eGFR sits more
    # than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR. Reference level is ">= -10%".
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat    = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10, "< -10%", ">= -10%"),
      levels = c(">= -10%", "< -10%")),
    # Stricter cut at -30 %: a much smaller, more clearly discordant group.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30, "< -30%", ">= -30%"),
      levels = c(">= -30%", "< -30%")),
    # Intermediate cut, between the primary -10 % and the stricter -30 %.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20, "< -20%", ">= -20%"),
      levels = c(">= -20%", "< -20%")),
    # Quartiles of the same continuous exposure. ntile() gives 1 to the most
    # negative quartile; Q4 (least discordant) is set as the reference level.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4     = factor(
      dplyr::ntile(egfr_diff_pct_sens, 4), levels = 4:1,
      labels = c("Q4 (least discordant)", "Q3", "Q2", "Q1 (most discordant)")),
    # "Survivor": still in follow-up beyond one year.
    survivor_365              = days_last_follow_up > 365,
    # Dose discrepancy uses CAPPED eGFR (already computed in ritu_data.qmd)
    dose_discrep_per25increase = dose_discrepancy / 25,
    abs_dose_discrep = abs(dose_discrepancy),
    abs_dose_discrep_cat = cut(abs_dose_discrep,
      breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<25", "25-49.99", "50-74.99", "75-99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    # Binary exposure for adjusted CIF curves (Section 14): 1 if patient was
    # over-dosed by 25 mg or more (actual - predicted >= 25), else 0.
    dose_discrep_ge25 = as.integer(dose_discrepancy >= 25),
    # Signed dose discrepancy = actual - predicted; 10 bins symmetric around 0.
    signed_dose_discrep_cat = cut(dose_discrepancy,
      breaks = c(-Inf, -100, -75, -50, -25, 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<=-100", "-99.99 to -75", "-74.99 to -50",
                 "-49.99 to -25", "-24.99 to 0",
                 "0 to 24.99", "25 to 49.99", "50 to 74.99",
                 "75 to 99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    cockcroft_per10 = cockcroft / 10,
    ckd_epi_per10   = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / 10
  )

cat("Carboplatin cohort N =", nrow(dat), "\n")

2 Dose Distribution (Carboplatin)

2.1 Actual vs Predicted Dose

Code 
dose_long <- dat %>%
  select(record_id, carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys),
    names_to = "dose_type", values_to = "dose_mg"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_mg)) %>%
  mutate(dose_type = case_match(dose_type,
    "carbo_dose_redcap"  ~ "Actual (REDCap)",
    "carbo_dose_cre_cys" ~ "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)"
  ))

ggplot(dose_long, aes(x = dose_mg, fill = dose_type)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.5, bins = 40, position = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Actual (REDCap)" = "#E31A1C",
                                "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)" = "#1F78B4")) +
  labs(title = "Carboplatin Dose Distribution",
       x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Dose Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

2.2 Signed Dose Discrepancy Distribution

Smooth kernel density estimate of the signed dose discrepancy (actual − predicted, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys). The area under the curve is shaded by sign — negative (under-dosed region) on one side, positive on the other.

Code 
dose_vals <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_discrepancy)) %>%
  pull(dose_discrepancy)

dens <- density(dose_vals, n = 512)
y_at_zero <- approx(dens$x, dens$y, xout = 0)$y

dens_df <- tibble(x = dens$x, y = dens$y) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(x = 0, y = y_at_zero)) %>%
  arrange(x)

neg_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x <= 0) %>% mutate(side = "neg")
pos_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x >= 0) %>% mutate(side = "pos")
plot_df  <- bind_rows(neg_part, pos_part)

ggplot() +
  geom_area(data = plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = side), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dens_df, aes(x = x, y = y), linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 25, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 250), ylim = c(0, 0.010)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Signed Dose Discrepancy (Carboplatin)",
       x = "Dose Discrepancy (mg) = Actual dose – Predicted dose",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

3.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)

Two alternative definitions of follow-up time shown side-by-side:

  • A — Raw days: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
  • B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was within 1 year of baseline.
Code 
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

fu_row <- function(label, v) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                  = label,
    N                               = length(v),
    `Median [IQR] follow-up (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(v)
  )
}

v <- followup_summary$days_last_follow_up
followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",             v),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days", v[v <= 365])
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (Carboplatin cohort). Two alternative definitions.") |>
  flextable::autofit()

3.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the ICI-CKD project and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management. Creatinine for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

None of these are censored at 90 days. A qualifying CKD episode has to be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up. aki is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all of them descriptively; aki and ckd_composite are the two that are modelled — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

Definitions as of the latest revision. aki is now restricted to events within 1 year of baseline (aki_any keeps the unrestricted count for reference and is not modelled). ckd_incidence uses a > 25 % eGFR drop; ckd_incidence_any drops the percent requirement entirely; ckd_progression now additionally requires a > 30 % further drop, where it previously counted any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD as progression and is why that count fell sharply.

aki is also not the same variable as AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median (or 2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation below shows how far the two diverge.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

3.3 Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs Baseline over Days 1-90 / 91-180 / 181-270 / 271-360

Change in creatinine eGFR from eGFR_CRE_baseline, using the median of every creatinine eGFR inside each window — days 1-90, 91-180, 181-270 and 271-360. Days run from baseline_sample_date. Built in Section 5.16b of Data Management.

Negative means decline. delta_egfr_d90 is eGFR at day 90 minus eGFR at baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number — the opposite sign to pct_drop in the data-management pipeline.

The windows are fixed and non-overlapping, so no measurement feeds two marks and every value drawn in a window counts toward it. A patient contributes to a window whenever they have at least one creatinine in it — the n column below shows how coverage falls off at the later windows.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
dgfr_marks <- c(90, 180, 270, 360)

dgfr_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(dgfr_marks, function(mk) {
  d  <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]
  dp <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mk)]]
  nv <- dat[[paste0("n_cre_d", mk)]]
  g  <- dat[[paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mk)]]
  ok <- !is.na(d)
  q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
         median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
  wl <- c("90" = "Days 1-90", "180" = "Days 91-180",
          "270" = "Days 181-270", "360" = "Days 271-360")
  tibble::tibble(
    Window = unname(wl[as.character(mk)]),
    n = sum(ok),
    `% with a value in window` = round(100 * sum(ok) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `Creatinines in window` = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]",
      median(nv[ok]), quantile(nv[ok], .25), quantile(nv[ok], .75)),
    `Median eGFR in window` = q3(g[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR` = q3(d[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR (%)` = q3(dp[ok])
  )
})

ft_dgfr <- flextable::flextable(dgfr_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(paste0(
    "Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline, N = %d. eGFR in mL/min/1.73m², ",
    "median [IQR] throughout. Negative = decline from baseline."), nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_dgfr, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec3_3_delta_egfr.docx"))

.iqr <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
}

why_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(0:3, function(k) {
  i <- .k == k
  tibble::tibble(
    `Marks covered` = paste0(k, " of 3"),
    n = sum(i),
    `% of cohort` = round(100 * sum(i) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `No post-baseline creatinine at all` = sum(i & dat$n_cre_post == 0),
    `Post-baseline creatinines, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$n_cre_post[i]),
    `Last creatinine, day, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$last_cre_days[i])
  )
})

4.2 eGFR Difference (sens) distribution

Signed eGFR difference (sens) = 100 × (CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C − CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine) / CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, both unindexed. Concordance sits at 0 %. Red bins are the negative side — cystatin C below creatinine, the muscle-wasting direction. The dotted line at − 30 % marks the strictest of the three cuts used for the binary exposures further down.

Code

4.4 CKD Stage Reclassification — Creatinine vs Creatinine + Cystatin C

Every patient carries two KDIGO G-stages, both built in Data Management: ckd_stage_cre from baseline_cre_egfr (CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine) and ckd_stage_cre_cys from ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys (CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C). Both are indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²), so the two stagings sit on the same scale and the move between them is read directly.

.stage_pal <- c("G1 (>=90)" = "#2E7D32", "G2 (60-89)" = "#1565C0",
                "G3a (45-59)" = "#EF6C00", "G3b (30-44)" = "#C62828",
                "G4 (15-29)" = "#6A1B9A", "G5 (<15)" = "#37474F")

# Hand-built Sankey: one polygon per creatinine-stage -> Cr-Cys-stage flow,
# node boxes scaled to their counts. Takes any staged subset, so the same
# figure can be redrawn on a sub-cohort without the code diverging.
.stage_sankey <- function(d, sub) {
  sk  <- d %>% count(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, name = "n")
  N   <- sum(sk$n)
  gap <- 0.055 * N

  # Node stacks: each stage a box, height proportional to n, separated by a gap.
  nodes <- function(col) sk %>%
    group_by(stage = .data[[col]]) %>% summarise(tot = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(stage) %>%
    mutate(ntop = lag(cumsum(tot), default = 0) + gap * (row_number() - 1),
           nbot = ntop + tot)
  ln <- nodes("ckd_stage_cre"); rn <- nodes("ckd_stage_cre_cys")

  lft <- sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
    group_by(ckd_stage_cre) %>%
    mutate(l0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), l1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(ln %>% select(ckd_stage_cre = stage, b = ntop), by = "ckd_stage_cre") %>%
    mutate(l0 = l0 + b, l1 = l1 + b)
  rgt <- sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre_cys, ckd_stage_cre) %>%
    group_by(ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
    mutate(r0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), r1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(rn %>% select(ckd_stage_cre_cys = stage, b = ntop),
              by = "ckd_stage_cre_cys") %>%
    mutate(r0 = r0 + b, r1 = r1 + b)

  fl <- lft %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, n, l0, l1) %>%
    left_join(rgt %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, r0, r1),
              by = c("ckd_stage_cre", "ckd_stage_cre_cys")) %>%
    mutate(flow = row_number(), pct = 100 * n / N)

  xlb <- 0.07; xle <- 0.22; xrb <- 0.78; xre <- 0.93
  tt <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 70); ease <- 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(pi * tt)

  # One polygon per flow: out along its top edge on a cosine ease, back along
  # the bottom. Tinted by the source stage so each origin stays traceable.
  rib <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
    list(fl$flow, fl$l0, fl$l1, fl$r0, fl$r1, as.character(fl$ckd_stage_cre)),
    function(id, l0, l1, r0, r1, src) tibble::tibble(
      flow = id, Stage = src,
      x = c(xle + (xrb - xle) * tt, xle + (xrb - xle) * rev(tt)),
      y = c(l0 + (r0 - l0) * ease, rev(l1 + (r1 - l1) * ease))))

  # Labels sit inside the box when it is tall enough, otherwise just outside it.
  nd <- dplyr::bind_rows(ln %>% mutate(xmin = xlb, xmax = xle),
                         rn %>% mutate(xmin = xrb, xmax = xre)) %>%
    mutate(big = tot >= 0.07 * N,
           lab = ifelse(big, sprintf("%s\n%d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / N),
                             sprintf("%s  %d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / N)),
           tx = ifelse(big, (xmin + xmax) / 2,
                       ifelse(xmin < 0.5, xmin - 0.012, xmax + 0.012)),
           hj = ifelse(big, 0.5, ifelse(xmin < 0.5, 1, 0)))

  fll <- fl %>% filter(pct >= 2.5) %>%
    mutate(lx = xle + 0.015, ly = (l0 + l1) / 2,
           rx = xrb - 0.015, ry = (r0 + r1) / 2, txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct))

  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = rib, aes(x, y, group = flow, fill = Stage),
                 alpha = 0.55, color = NA) +
    geom_rect(data = nd, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ntop, ymax = nbot,
                             fill = stage), color = NA) +
    geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(nd, big),
              aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
              color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.95) +
    geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(nd, !big),
              aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
              color = "grey15", size = 2.8) +
    geom_text(data = fll, aes(lx, ly, label = txt), hjust = 0, size = 2.9,
              color = "grey20") +
    geom_text(data = fll, aes(rx, ry, label = txt), hjust = 1, size = 2.9,
              color = "grey20") +
    annotate("text", x = c((xlb + xle) / 2, (xrb + xre) / 2),
             y = -0.055 * max(nd$nbot), fontface = "bold", size = 4.1,
             label = c("CKD-EPI creatinine", "CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = .stage_pal, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.11, 0.04))) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 1.15), expand = expansion(mult = 0.005)) +
    labs(title = "CKD stage: creatinine eGFR vs creatinine + cystatin C eGFR",
         subtitle = sub, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

5 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (unindexed, mL/min) (Carboplatin)

These are the only two outcomes modelled on this page. Both run on the long-horizon kidney outcomes built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management: AKI is administratively censored at 365 days, the CKD composite runs to the last creatinine (day 0 → last follow-up). Death at any time is the competing event in both, taken from death_days_any rather than the 90-day death_90 flag, which cannot place a death in time beyond day 90. death_days_any is the union of the two sources that carry a death date — the RPDR Date_Of_Death when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up date for a patient REDCap records as dead. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored.

The exposure in both sections below is egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10 — 100 × (eGFR_CysC − eGFR_Cr) / eGFR_Cr, negated and divided by 10, so every subdistribution hazard ratio reads per 10 percentage-point decline. Cystatin C against creatinine alone, both unindexed. The two sections differ only in the kidney adjuster: creatinine eGFR in absolute mL/min here, indexed to body surface area in the next. All other adjusters are the project’s standard set (Section 1).

Each table shows univariable (one variable at a time) and multivariable Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratios side-by-side. A Word version of each table is saved during render — the download link sits under its heading.

Code 
.adj_set <- function(pre_labs, egfr_adj) {
  adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
           "cancer_type_cat_7","high_dose",
           "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
           "bmi","smoking","thyroid")
  if (egfr_adj == "cockcroft") adj <- c(adj, "cockcroft")
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi")   adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex")
  # Indexed to BSA (mL/min/1.73m2), as opposed to the absolute mL/min above.
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi_idx") adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys")
  # Creatinine-only CKD-EPI 2021, race-free. Unlike the Cr-Cys forms above
  # it shares no measurement with the exposure.
  if (egfr_adj == "cre")     adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed")
  if (egfr_adj == "cre_idx") adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) adj <- c(adj, pre_labs)
  adj
}

# fg_model: returns univariable + multivariable merged Fine-Gray table.
# If docx_name is supplied, also saves the table as a .docx in docx_dir.
fg_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                     egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                     docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- tidycmprsk::crr(fmla_mv, failcode = 1, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = tidycmprsk::crr,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3),
      method.args = list(failcode = 1)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_model <- .wrap_tbl(fg_model)


cox_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                      egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                      docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- survival::coxph(fmla_mv, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = survival::coxph,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_model <- .wrap_tbl(cox_model)

6 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²) (Carboplatin)

Identical to the section above in every respect but one: the kidney adjuster is baseline_cre_egfr — CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area, mL/min/1.73m² — where the section above uses baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed, the same estimate in absolute mL/min.

Same exposure (egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10, per 10 percentage-point decline), same two outcomes, same competing event, same remaining covariates. The two sections therefore isolate what the BSA indexing of the adjuster does. The two forms correlate at 0.86, so they are related but not interchangeable.

Cockcroft-Gault is no longer an adjuster in either section.

7 Survivors Cohort — Follow-up > 365 Days (Carboplatin)

The Fine-Gray models above, rerun on patients still in follow-up beyond one year (days_last_follow_up > 365). Adjusted for baseline_cre_egfr (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²); same exposure and competing event, only the cohort changes.

This conditions on a post-baseline characteristic. Surviving and staying in follow-up past a year is partly a consequence of the kidney trajectory being modelled, so this subset is not a random sample and these estimates are not directly comparable with the full-cohort ones above. Read it as a restriction analysis, not a sensitivity analysis.

Code 
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

surv_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  Outcome  = c("AKI within 1 year", "CKD composite (any time)"),
  Censored = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 0), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 0)),
  Event    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 1), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1)),
  Death    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 2), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 2))
)
knitr::kable(surv_counts, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients (%.1f %%). Competing-risk event counts.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort), 100 * nrow(dat) / nrow(dat_full_cohort)))

Code 
dat <- dat_full_cohort

8 Binary eGFR Difference (sens) — AKI and CKD Composite (Carboplatin)

The same two outcomes and the same adjusters as the Fine-Gray sections above, with the exposure entered as a binary split rather than per 10 percentage-point decline.

  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat splits at − 10 % — < -10% means the cystatin C eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; >= -10% is the reference.
  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20 splits at − 20 %, an intermediate cut.
  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 splits at − 30 %, a smaller and more clearly discordant group.

Each subdistribution hazard ratio is therefore for the exposed group against its reference group, not per unit. Death at any time is the competing event and the kidney adjuster is baseline_cre_egfr (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²), as in the sections above.

8.1 Prevalence of the three cuts

Code 
.cut_row <- function(v, lab) tibble::tibble(
  Cut = lab, Exposed = sum(v), Unexposed = sum(!v),
  `% exposed` = round(100 * mean(v), 1),
  `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[v]  == 1),
  `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!v] == 1),
  `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[v]  == 1),
  `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!v] == 1))

cut_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat   == "< -10%", "< -10% (primary)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20 == "< -20%", "< -20% (intermediate)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 == "< -30%", "< -30% (stricter)"))

knitr::kable(cut_tbl, caption = sprintf(
  "Prevalence of the three binary cuts, N = %d. Median eGFR difference (sens) %.1f %%.",
  nrow(dat), median(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens, na.rm = TRUE)))

The six models above, repeated on the survivors cohort (days_last_follow_up > 365). Same exposures, outcomes, adjusters and competing event; only the cohort changes. As in the survivors section earlier, this conditions on a post-baseline characteristic, so these are a restriction analysis rather than a sensitivity check.

Code 
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

binsurv <- purrr::map_dfr(
  list(c("< -10%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat"),
       c("< -20%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20"),
       c("< -30%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30")),
  function(z) {
    e <- dat[[z[2]]] == z[1]
    tibble::tibble(Cut = z[1], `n survivors` = nrow(dat),
                   Exposed = sum(e), Unexposed = sum(!e),
                   `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[e]  == 1),
                   `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!e] == 1),
                   `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[e]  == 1),
                   `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!e] == 1))
  })
knitr::kable(binsurv, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients. Exposed-group event counts behind the six models below.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort)))

10 Paper (Carboplatin)

A total of 47 (24.9%) patients received an excess dose of carboplatin, defined as ≥ 25 mg higher than the dose that would have been predicted using the CKD-EPI eGFRCR-CYS equation adjusted for actual BSA.

(Denominator: 189 carboplatin patients with a computable predicted dose.)

11 360-Day Delta eGFR on the Binary eGFR Difference (sens) (Carboplatin)

The outcome is delta_egfr_d360 — the median creatinine eGFR over days 271-360 minus baseline, in mL/min/1.73m², negative = decline (see the Delta eGFR table above). Only patients with at least one creatinine in that window contribute, so every model in this section is complete-case on that variable and its n is well below the cohort.

Both cuts of egfr_diff_pct_sens are reported: the primary one at − 10 % and the stricter one at − 30 %. < -10% means the cystatin C eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; >= -10% is the reference level.

11.1 360-day delta eGFR by group — cut at − 10 %

Code 
.grp_row <- function(d, lab) {
  v <- d$delta_egfr_d360[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_d360)]
  p <- d$delta_egfr_pct_d360[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_pct_d360)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Group = lab, n = length(v),
    `Delta eGFR, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(v), sd(v)),
    `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(v), quantile(v, .25), quantile(v, .75)),
    `Delta eGFR %, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(p), quantile(p, .25), quantile(p, .75)))
}
d0 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == ">= -10%")
d1 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == "< -10%")
grp_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(.grp_row(d0, ">= -10% (reference)"), .grp_row(d1, "< -10%"))

.wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(delta_egfr_d360 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
.tt <- tryCatch(t.test(delta_egfr_d360 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(grp_tbl), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "360-day delta eGFR by binary eGFR difference (sens). Negative = decline. ",
  "Wilcoxon p = %s; Welch t-test p = %s."),
  if (is.null(.wt)) "—" else format.pval(.wt$p.value, digits = 3),
  if (is.null(.tt)) "—" else format.pval(.tt$p.value, digits = 3)))

11.2 Linear model — cut at − 10 % (Carboplatin, all patients)

Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models, including the same kidney adjuster — baseline_cre_egfr, CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of 365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on < -10% means that group declined further.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d360 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "cre_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d360 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d360", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d360,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d360 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d360)

lm_d360("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec11_lm_d360")

12 Quartiles of eGFR Difference (sens) as the Exposure (Carboplatin)

The same continuous exposure as the Fine-Gray sections above, entered as quartiles instead of a binary cut or a per-10-point slope. egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4 is built with dplyr::ntile(), so Q1 holds the most discordant quarter (cystatin C furthest below creatinine) and Q4 the least. Q4 is the reference level, so each ratio reads against the least discordant quarter and a value above 1 means more discordance carries more risk.

Same two outcomes, same competing event (death at any time), same multivariable set and the same kidney adjuster baseline_cre_egfr as everywhere else on this page. Three dummy terms replace one, so these models spend two more degrees of freedom than the binary ones on the same events.

12.1 Quartile boundaries and event counts

Code 
q_tbl <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4)) %>%
  group_by(Quartile = egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Range (%)` = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f",
                                  min(egfr_diff_pct_sens), max(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `Median (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", median(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `AKI events` = sum(cmp_status_aki_365 == 1),
            `CKD events` = sum(cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(q_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Quartiles of eGFR difference (sens), N = %d with a non-missing value. ",
  "Q4 (least discordant) is the reference level in every model below."),
  sum(!is.na(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4))))

12.6 Adjusted Cumulative Incidence — AKI within 1 Year (Carboplatin, all patients)

Section 12.2 reports subdistribution hazard ratios; these curves give the absolute risk the same fit implies. They are model-standardised: every patient in the analysis set is assigned to one quartile in turn, their cumulative incidence is predicted from the adjusted Fine-Gray model, and the predictions are averaged across the cohort. A curve is therefore the incidence the whole cohort would show if all of it sat in that quartile with the covariate mix held fixed — not the observed curve of the patients who happen to fall in it. Death is the competing event, so these are cumulative incidence functions, not 1 − Kaplan-Meier.

The band is a pointwise 95 % interval from 500 bootstrap resamples of the patients, each one refitted and re-standardised. It carries no multiplicity correction and is not a test of the gap between quartiles — that is the p-value in the Section 12.2 table.

Code 
CIF_BOOT <- 500   # bootstrap resamples behind the pointwise band

PAL_Q4 <- c("Q4 (least discordant)" = "#1F78B4", "Q3"                   = "#A6CEE3",
            "Q2"                    = "#FDBF6F", "Q1 (most discordant)" = "#E31A1C")

# g-formula standardisation. Set the quartile dummies of the fitted design
# matrix to one level for every patient, predict each patient's CIF, average
# over the cohort, then read the step function onto a common time grid so
# bootstrap replicates with different event times can be stacked.
.cif_std <- function(fitobj, lv, tg, pred) {
  X <- as.matrix(stats::model.matrix(fitobj))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(lv), function(i) {
    Xq <- X
    Xq[, grep(paste0("^", pred), colnames(Xq))] <- 0
    nm <- paste0(pred, lv[i])
    if (nm %in% colnames(Xq)) Xq[, nm] <- 1
    pr <- stats::predict(fitobj$cmprsk, cov1 = Xq)
    tibble::tibble(Quartile = factor(lv[i], levels = lv), time = tg,
      cif = stats::approx(pr[, 1], rowMeans(pr[, -1, drop = FALSE]),
                          xout = tg, method = "constant", f = 0,
                          yleft = 0, rule = 2)$y)
  }))
}

# Fit the adjusted Fine-Gray model exactly as fg_model() does, standardise it,
# and bootstrap the whole pipeline for the band.
.cif_q4 <- function(time_var, status_var, d = dat, boot = CIF_BOOT) {
  pred <- "egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4"
  # .adj_set() takes pred_var on the whole / entire pages and not on the
  # carboplatin ones, so call whichever signature this page defines.
  adj  <- if ("pred_var" %in% names(formals(.adj_set)))
            .adj_set(pred, NULL, "cre_idx") else .adj_set(NULL, "cre_idx")
  cc <- d %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(c(time_var, status_var, pred, adj)))
  fml <- stats::as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
                                  paste(c(pred, adj), collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- tidycmprsk::crr(fml, failcode = 1, data = cc)
  lv  <- levels(droplevels(cc[[pred]]))
  tg  <- seq(0, max(cc[[time_var]][cc[[status_var]] != 0]), length.out = 200)
  est <- .cif_std(fit, lv, tg, pred)
  nrw <- length(lv) * length(tg)
  bs  <- vapply(seq_len(boot), function(b) tryCatch({
      i <- sample.int(nrow(cc), nrow(cc), replace = TRUE)
      .cif_std(tidycmprsk::crr(fml, failcode = 1, data = cc[i, ]), lv, tg, pred)$cif
    }, error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, nrw)), numeric(nrw))
  ok <- colSums(is.na(bs)) == 0
  est$lo <- if (any(ok)) apply(bs[, ok, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::quantile, .025) else NA_real_
  est$hi <- if (any(ok)) apply(bs[, ok, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::quantile, .975) else NA_real_
  attr(est, "meta") <- list(n = nrow(cc), ev = sum(cc[[status_var]] == 1),
                            cmp = sum(cc[[status_var]] == 2), nb = sum(ok))
  est
}

.cif_plot <- function(x, ttl, sub) {
  m  <- attr(x, "meta")
  en <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(Quartile) %>% dplyr::slice_max(time, n = 1) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  # A bootstrap band that spans most of the 0-100 % range carries no
  # information and squashes the curves against the floor of the panel. Drop
  # it and say so, rather than draw a figure that cannot be read.
  bw   <- stats::median(x$hi - x$lo, na.rm = TRUE)
  wide <- !is.finite(bw) || bw > 0.5
  note <- if (!is.finite(bw))
      "Model-standardised; band omitted, the bootstrap did not converge"
    else if (wide)
      sprintf("Model-standardised; band omitted, %d bootstraps span %.0f points",
              m$nb, 100 * bw)
    else
      sprintf("Model-standardised; band = pointwise 95%% from %d bootstraps", m$nb)
  ggplot(x, aes(time, cif, color = Quartile, fill = Quartile)) +
    (if (wide) NULL else
       geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.13, color = NA)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = en, aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * cif)),
      direction = "y", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 6, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
      segment.color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = PAL_Q4) + scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_Q4) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.09))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(title = ttl, subtitle = sprintf("%s | N = %d, %d events, %d competing deaths\n%s",
           sub, m$n, m$ev, m$cmp, note),
         x = "Days from baseline", y = "Adjusted cumulative incidence",
         color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

.cif_fig <- .wrap_plot(function(time_var, status_var, ttl, sub)
  .cif_plot(.cif_q4(time_var, status_var), ttl, sub))

13 Linear Mixed Model — Creatinine eGFR Slope over Days 0-360 (Carboplatin)

What this section adds. The 360-Day Delta eGFR section compares one number per patient: the median creatinine eGFR over days 271-360 minus baseline. That needs a creatinine in the final window, which only part of the cohort has, so those models are complete-case on a single difference. This section instead fits a linear mixed model to every creatinine eGFR in days 0-360, so each patient contributes whatever measurements they have and nobody is dropped for missing the last window. Both are kept — they answer related but different questions, and it is worth seeing whether they agree.

Data. One row per creatinine eGFR. Day 0 is eGFR_CRE_baseline; every later row is a post-baseline creatinine inside days 1-360, read from ritu_cre_traj.rds (Section 5.16b of Data Management). Patients with no post-baseline creatinine in that span are not in the model. Time is in years (time_yr = day / 365), so every coefficient below is mL/min/1.73m² per year and negative means decline.

Model. eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * group + covariates + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)

  • time_yr × group is the estimand — the difference in annual eGFR slope between each exposure level and the reference level.
  • group on its own is the day-0 difference between the levels.
  • (1 + time_yr | EMPI) gives each patient a random intercept and a random slope, with an unstructured 2 × 2 covariance so the model can let patients who start lower decline faster or slower. Residuals are independent (σ²I); the random slope already induces within-patient correlation that grows with time separation. Fitted by REML in lme4, p-values by Satterthwaite from lmerTest.
  • Covariates are main effects only. They adjust the day-0 level, not the slope; only the exposure is allowed to interact with time. The covariate set is otherwise the same one the Fine-Gray models use.
  • baseline_cre_egfr is deliberately left out. Day 0 of the outcome is the baseline creatinine eGFR, so adjusting for it would mean conditioning on the outcome’s own first observation; the random intercept already absorbs where each patient starts. Everywhere else on this page the kidney adjuster is still baseline_cre_egfr.
  • The slope is one straight line across days 0-360. The observed group means are close to flat for the first six months and then fall (Section 3.3), so a single line averages an early plateau with a later decline. Read it as the average rate over the year, not as a constant one.

The Unadjusted column fits the same model with no covariates, on the same patients as the adjusted model, so the two columns are directly comparable.

13.1 Trajectory data behind these models

Code 
# Long-format creatinine eGFR, one row per post-baseline value in days 1-360.
# Written by ritu_data.qmd, which keeps it out of the one-row-per-patient
# masters. Keyed by EMPI only, so this page joins its own cohort to it.
lmm_traj_all <- readRDS("ritu_cre_traj.rds")

LMM_CTL <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

# Build the long frame for one model: the cohort's patient-level columns, a
# day-0 row carrying eGFR_CRE_baseline, then every post-baseline value. The
# day-0 anchor is eGFR_CRE_baseline, not baseline_cre_egfr -- the latter comes
# off a different creatinine draw and is not on this trajectory's scale.
.lmm_data <- function(d, vars) {
  pat <- d %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(unique(c("EMPI", "eGFR_CRE_baseline", vars)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline)) %>%
    dplyr::semi_join(lmm_traj_all, by = "EMPI")
  post <- pat %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(lmm_traj_all %>% dplyr::select(EMPI, cre_day, eGFR_CRE),
                      by = "EMPI")
  dplyr::bind_rows(pat %>% mutate(cre_day = 0, eGFR_CRE = eGFR_CRE_baseline),
                   post) %>%
    dplyr::select(-eGFR_CRE_baseline) %>%
    mutate(time_yr = cre_day / 365) %>%
    arrange(EMPI, cre_day)
}

# egfr_adj = "none" leaves every kidney term out of the adjuster set.
.lmm_fits <- function(pred_var) {
  adj <- .adj_for(pred_var, "none")
  d   <- .lmm_data(dat, c(pred_var, adj))
  rhs <- paste0("eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ", pred_var)
  list(pred = pred_var,
       un = lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0(rhs, " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")),
                           data = d, control = LMM_CTL),
       ad = lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0(rhs, " + ",
              paste(adj, collapse = " + "), " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")),
              data = d, control = LMM_CTL))
}

lmm_slope <- function(pred_var, docx_name = NULL) {
  m  <- .lmm_fits(pred_var)
  tb <- function(x) tbl_regression(
    x, pvalue_fun = function(p) style_pvalue(p, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tb(m$un), tb(m$ad)),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Unadjusted**", "**Adjusted**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  attr(out, "lmm") <- m
  out
}
lmm_slope <- .wrap_tbl(lmm_slope)

# Group-specific annual slopes implied by the adjusted fixed effects: the
# reference slope is b[time_yr], each other level's is b[time_yr] plus its
# interaction term. SEs come from the fixed-effect covariance matrix; the
# p-value is the Satterthwaite test on the interaction. Returns nothing for a
# continuous exposure (no groups) or when the fit failed and .wrap_tbl caught it.
.lmm_slope_tbl <- function(x) {
  m <- attr(x, "lmm")
  if (is.null(m)) return(invisible(NULL))
  fit <- m$ad; pred <- m$pred
  mf  <- stats::model.frame(fit)
  if (!is.factor(mf[[pred]])) return(invisible(NULL))
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); V <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(fit)); nm <- names(b)
  cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  it <- which(startsWith(nm, paste0("time_yr:", pred)))
  fmt <- function(cv) {
    e <- sum(cv * b); s <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(cv) %*% V %*% cv))
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", e, e - 1.96 * s, e + 1.96 * s)
  }
  t0 <- as.numeric(nm == "time_yr"); lv <- levels(mf[[pred]])
  rows <- list(tibble::tibble(
    Group = paste0(lv[1], " (reference)"),
    `eGFR slope, mL/min/1.73m² per year` = fmt(t0),
    `Difference vs reference` = "—", `p-value` = "—"))
  for (k in seq_along(it)) {
    cv <- t0; cv[it[k]] <- 1
    dv <- as.numeric(seq_along(nm) == it[k])
    rows[[k + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
      Group = sub(paste0("^time_yr:", pred), "", nm[it[k]]),
      `eGFR slope, mL/min/1.73m² per year` = fmt(cv),
      `Difference vs reference` = fmt(dv),
      `p-value` = style_pvalue(cf[nm[it[k]], "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3))
  }
  knitr::kable(dplyr::bind_rows(rows), caption = sprintf(paste0(
    "Adjusted annual creatinine eGFR slope by group. Negative = decline. ",
    "N = %d patients, %d eGFR values including the day-0 baseline. ",
    "The p-value tests the time x group interaction (Satterthwaite)."),
    as.integer(lme4::ngrps(fit)), stats::nobs(fit)))
}

13.2 Observed trajectories and fitted slopes — cut at − 10 % (Carboplatin, all patients)

Points are raw mean creatinine eGFR in 60-day bins (day 0 shown on its own), with a 95 % CI (mean ± 1.96 × SE); bins holding fewer than 11 values are suppressed. Lines are the fitted population slopes from the unadjusted mixed model. The points are cross-sectional means, so which patients contribute changes from bin to bin — the lines, which use each patient’s whole trajectory, are the estimate; the points are only there to show the raw data behind it.

Code 
.lmm_traj_plot <- function(pred_var, ttl) {
  adj <- .adj_for(pred_var, "none")
  d   <- .lmm_data(dat, c(pred_var, adj)) %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[pred_var]]))
  fit <- lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0("eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ", pred_var,
           " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")), data = d, control = LMM_CTL)
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); lv <- levels(d[[pred_var]])
  ln <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(lv), function(k) {
    a <- b[["(Intercept)"]]; s <- b[["time_yr"]]
    if (k > 1) {
      a <- a + b[[paste0(pred_var, lv[k])]]
      s <- s + b[[paste0("time_yr:", pred_var, lv[k])]]
    }
    tibble::tibble(grp = factor(lv[k], levels = lv), cre_day = c(0, 360),
                   fit = a + s * c(0, 360) / 365)
  }))
  obs <- d %>%
    mutate(grp = .data[[pred_var]],
           mid = ifelse(cre_day == 0, 0,
                        pmin(floor(cre_day / 60), 5) * 60 + 30)) %>%
    group_by(grp, mid) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(eGFR_CRE), se = sd(eGFR_CRE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
              k = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(k >= 11)   # small-cell suppression
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = ln, aes(cre_day, fit, color = grp), linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = obs, aes(mid, ymin = m - 1.96 * se,
                                  ymax = m + 1.96 * se, color = grp),
                  width = 8, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = obs, aes(mid, m, color = grp), size = 2.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("grey35", "#E31A1C", "#1F78B4", "#33A02C"),
                       name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 360, 60)) +
    labs(title = ttl, x = "Days from baseline",
         y = "Creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
.lmm_traj_plot <- .wrap_plot(.lmm_traj_plot)

.lmm_traj_plot("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat",
               "Creatinine eGFR over the first year, by eGFR difference (sens)")

13.11 Mixed model — continuous exposure (Carboplatin, all patients)

egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10 is the continuous exposure on the per-10-percentage-point decline scale, the same one the Fine-Gray models use. The time_yr × egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10 coefficient is the change in annual eGFR slope per 10 percentage points further the cystatin C eGFR sits below the creatinine eGFR. There is no group table for a continuous exposure.

14 CKD Stage Reclassification — eGFR Trends (Carboplatin)

The question. Everyone carries two baseline CKD stages: one from the creatinine eGFR (ckd_stage_cre, from baseline_cre_egfr) and one from the CKD-EPI creatinine–cystatin C eGFR (ckd_stage_cre_cys, from ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys), both indexed to BSA. The Sankey in the distributions section shows who moves between them. This section asks what happens next: does the creatinine eGFR fall faster in the patients cystatin C reclassifies into a worse stage?

Two groupings.

  1. Eight groups — within each baseline creatinine stage G1 to G3b, split by whether the Cr-Cys stage is the same or better, or worse. G4 and G5 by creatinine are not split this way; there are too few.
  2. Two groups, across every creatinine stage — same or better by Cr-Cys against reclassified worse by Cr-Cys.

What is plotted. Mean creatinine eGFR with a 95 % confidence interval (mean ± 1.96 × SE) at baseline and at each of the four windows — eGFR_CRE_baseline, then the medians over days 1-90, 91-180, 181-270 and 271-360 built in Section 3.3. The y axis is the creatinine eGFR throughout; serial cystatin C is not available, so the Cr-Cys stage is a baseline grouping, not a repeated measure.

Read the lines with the composition in mind. Each point is a cross-sectional mean of whoever had a creatinine in that window, and coverage falls from about 99 % in the first window to about 63 % in the last (Section 3.3). So a line can move because patients declined or because a different set of patients contributed. The mixed models in the previous section are the within-patient version of the same question.

Small cells are suppressed. A group is plotted only when at least 11 patients have a baseline value, and a later mark is omitted when it falls below 11 — so a line can stop early. Each plot names what was dropped.

14.1 Group definitions and sizes

Code 
# Canonical stage order, independent of which levels survive droplevels() in a
# cohort, so the groupings are built by position rather than by factor level.
CKD_LV      <- c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3a (45-59)", "G3b (30-44)",
                 "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")
CKD_SHORT   <- c("G1", "G2", "G3a", "G3b", "G4", "G5")
TREND_MIN_N <- 11

# Labels mirror the requested list: within creatinine stage i, "same or better"
# is Cr-Cys stage <= i and "worse" is >= i+1. ASCII >= / <= throughout, matching
# the stage names themselves.
.lab_same  <- function(i) if (i == 1) "G1 cre, G1 by Cr-Cys" else
  sprintf("%s cre, <=%s by Cr-Cys", CKD_SHORT[i], CKD_SHORT[i])
.lab_worse <- function(i)
  sprintf("%s cre, >=%s by Cr-Cys", CKD_SHORT[i], CKD_SHORT[i + 1])

.ckd_groups <- function(d) {
  ci    <- match(as.character(d$ckd_stage_cre),     CKD_LV)
  yi    <- match(as.character(d$ckd_stage_cre_cys), CKD_LV)
  worse <- yi > ci
  d$ckd_shift2 <- factor(
    ifelse(worse, "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys", "Same or better by Cr-Cys"),
    levels = c("Same or better by Cr-Cys", "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"))
  lab <- ifelse(worse,
    vapply(ci, function(i) if (is.na(i)) NA_character_ else .lab_worse(i), ""),
    vapply(ci, function(i) if (is.na(i)) NA_character_ else .lab_same(i), ""))
  lab[is.na(ci) | ci > 4] <- NA        # the eight groups stop at G3b
  d$ckd_shift8 <- factor(lab, levels = unlist(lapply(1:4,
                    function(i) c(.lab_same(i), .lab_worse(i)))))
  d
}

TREND_MARKS <- c(BL = "eGFR_CRE_baseline", "90" = "eGFR_CRE_d90",
                 "180" = "eGFR_CRE_d180", "270" = "eGFR_CRE_d270",
                 "360" = "eGFR_CRE_d360")

# Day each window closes, used to stop carrying forward at death.
TREND_CLOSE <- c(BL = 0, "90" = 90, "180" = 180, "270" = 270, "360" = 360)

# Last observation carried forward: a patient with no creatinine inside a window
# keeps the value from their most recent earlier window. Baseline is present for
# everyone in a group, so after carrying the only patients still absent from a
# mark are those who died on or before it. kc counts how many of a mark's values
# are carried rather than measured in that window.
.trend_stats <- function(d, grp_var) {
  mk <- names(TREND_MARKS)
  v  <- lapply(TREND_MARKS, function(cl) d[[cl]])
  names(v) <- mk
  dd <- if ("death_days_any" %in% names(d)) d$death_days_any else
          rep(NA_real_, nrow(d))
  cf <- stats::setNames(lapply(mk, function(.) rep(FALSE, nrow(d))), mk)
  for (j in seq_along(mk)[-1]) {
    g <- is.na(v[[j]]) & !is.na(v[[j - 1]]) &
         (is.na(dd) | dd > TREND_CLOSE[[mk[j]]])
    v[[j]][g]  <- v[[j - 1]][g]
    cf[[j]][g] <- TRUE
  }
  st <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mk), function(j)
      tibble::tibble(grp = d[[grp_var]], day = mk[j],
                     egfr = v[[j]], carried = cf[[j]]))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(grp), !is.na(egfr)) %>%
    mutate(day = factor(day, levels = mk)) %>%
    group_by(grp, day) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(egfr), se = sd(egfr) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
              k = dplyr::n(), kc = sum(carried), .groups = "drop")
  keep <- st %>% filter(day == "BL", k >= TREND_MIN_N) %>% pull(grp)
  list(stats   = st %>% filter(grp %in% keep, k >= TREND_MIN_N) %>% droplevels(),
       dropped = st %>% filter(day == "BL", k < TREND_MIN_N) %>%
                   transmute(grp = as.character(grp), n = k),
       thin    = sum(st$grp %in% keep & st$k < TREND_MIN_N))
}

PAL8 <- c(G1 = "#1F78B4", G2 = "#33A02C", G3a = "#FF7F00", G3b = "#E31A1C")
PAL2 <- c("Same or better by Cr-Cys" = "#1F78B4",
          "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys" = "#E31A1C")

# by_stage = TRUE colours by creatinine stage and dashes the reclassified-worse
# line, so the eight groups read as four pairs.
trend_plot <- function(grp_var, ttl, by_stage = FALSE) {
  r  <- .trend_stats(.ckd_groups(dat), grp_var)
  st <- r$stats
  if (!nrow(st)) stop("no group reaches the minimum cell size in this cohort")
  st <- st %>% mutate(
    cre   = factor(sub(" cre.*", "", as.character(grp)), levels = CKD_SHORT),
    shift = ifelse(grepl(">=", as.character(grp), fixed = TRUE),
                   "Worse by Cr-Cys", "Same or better"))
  note <- c(
    paste("Last observation carried forward: a patient with no creatinine in a",
          "window keeps their most recent earlier value, and carrying stops at",
          "death. Bracketed counts in the table below are carried values."),
    if (nrow(r$dropped)) sprintf("Not plotted, fewer than %d patients: %s.",
      TREND_MIN_N, paste(sprintf("%s (n = %d)", r$dropped$grp, r$dropped$n),
                         collapse = "; ")),
    if (r$thin) sprintf("%d later mark(s) also fall below %d and are omitted.",
                        r$thin, TREND_MIN_N))
  key <- if (by_stage) "cre" else "grp"
  p <- ggplot(st, aes(day, m, group = grp, colour = .data[[key]])) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se),
                  width = .12, linewidth = .5) +
    {if (by_stage) geom_line(aes(linetype = shift), linewidth = .9)
     else geom_line(linewidth = .9)} +
    geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = if (by_stage) PAL8 else PAL2,
                        name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
    labs(title = ttl, x = "Days from baseline",
         y = "Creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²)", linetype = NULL,
         caption = if (length(note)) paste(
           strwrap(paste(note, collapse = " "), width = 115), collapse = "\n")
           else NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
  attr(p, "counts") <- st %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cell = ifelse(kc > 0, sprintf("%d (%d)", k, kc),
                                as.character(k))) %>%
    dplyr::select(grp, day, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = day, values_from = cell) %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group = grp)
  p
}
trend_plot <- .wrap_plot(trend_plot)

# Per-mark n behind the plot above it. Silent when the plot failed to build.
trend_counts <- function(p) {
  k <- attr(p, "counts")
  if (is.null(k)) return(invisible(NULL))
  # The cells are strings now ("215 (69)"), and kable's na= does not blank a
  # character column, so clear the suppressed ones here.
  k[] <- lapply(k, function(cl) {
    cl <- as.character(cl); cl[is.na(cl)] <- ""; cl })
  knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(k, "counts"), caption = paste0(
    "Patients contributing to each mark; (n) = how many of them carry forward ",
    "an earlier window's value rather than one measured in that window. ",
    "Blank = fewer than ", TREND_MIN_N, " and not plotted."))
}

.cnt <- function(a, b, v) {
  ta <- table(a[[v]]); tb <- table(b[[v]])
  tibble::tibble(Group = names(ta), `All patients` = as.integer(ta),
                 Survivors = as.integer(tb[names(ta)])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Survivors = ifelse(is.na(Survivors), 0L, Survivors),
                  Plotted = ifelse(`All patients` >= TREND_MIN_N, "yes", "no"))
}

15 Baseline-Matched eGFR Trends (Carboplatin)

The Section 14 plots start from different levels: inside every baseline creatinine stage the reclassified-worse group sits lower, because cystatin C pushes a patient out of a stage band most easily when they already sit near its floor. A difference in where two lines end is therefore partly a difference in where they began. This section repeats those four plots on a matched cohort, so each pair of lines starts from the same baseline creatinine eGFR.

Code 
MATCH_CAL <- 2   # caliper on baseline creatinine eGFR, mL/min/1.73m2

# Greedy 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on baseline creatinine eGFR. Each
# reclassified-worse patient takes the same-or-better patient closest to it,
# among those inside MATCH_CAL and in the same baseline creatinine CKD stage.
# Controls are used once. Treated patients with the fewest eligible controls go
# first, which maximises the number of pairs. Returns the matched rows only.
.match_bl <- function(d) {
  g  <- .ckd_groups(d)
  ci <- match(as.character(g$ckd_stage_cre), CKD_LV)
  bl <- g$eGFR_CRE_baseline
  w  <- !is.na(g$ckd_shift2) &
        g$ckd_shift2 == "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"
  ok <- !is.na(ci) & ci <= 4 & !is.na(bl) & !is.na(g$ckd_shift2)
  tr <- which(ok & w); co <- which(ok & !w)
  if (!length(tr) || !length(co)) return(g[0, , drop = FALSE])
  elig <- lapply(tr, function(i)
    co[abs(bl[co] - bl[i]) <= MATCH_CAL & ci[co] == ci[i]])
  names(elig) <- as.character(tr)
  used <- integer(0); a <- integer(0); b <- integer(0)
  for (i in tr[order(lengths(elig))]) {
    cand <- setdiff(elig[[as.character(i)]], used)
    if (!length(cand)) next
    pick <- cand[which.min(abs(bl[cand] - bl[i]))]
    used <- c(used, pick); a <- c(a, i); b <- c(b, pick)
  }
  if (!length(a)) return(g[0, , drop = FALSE])
  out <- g[c(a, b), , drop = FALSE]
  out$.pair_id <- rep(seq_along(a), 2)
  out
}

# Baseline creatinine eGFR in the two groups before and after matching, with the
# standardised mean difference.
.match_balance <- function(d) {
  sm <- function(x, y) (mean(x) - mean(y)) / sqrt((var(x) + var(y)) / 2)
  row <- function(lbl, f) {
    if (!nrow(f)) return(NULL)
    w <- f$ckd_shift2 == "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"
    a <- f$eGFR_CRE_baseline[w & !is.na(f$eGFR_CRE_baseline)]
    b <- f$eGFR_CRE_baseline[!w & !is.na(f$eGFR_CRE_baseline)]
    if (length(a) < 2 || length(b) < 2) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(Set = lbl,
      `Worse n` = length(a), `Worse mean` = round(mean(a), 1),
      `Same or better n` = length(b), `Same or better mean` = round(mean(b), 1),
      Difference = round(mean(a) - mean(b), 1), SMD = round(sm(a, b), 3))
  }
  g <- .ckd_groups(d) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ckd_shift2), !is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline),
           !is.na(match(as.character(ckd_stage_cre), CKD_LV[1:4])))
  dplyr::bind_rows(row("Before matching", g),
                   row("After matching",  .match_bl(d)))
}
.match_balance <- .wrap_tbl(.match_balance)

15.1 Matching method

  1. Eligible patients — baseline creatinine CKD stage G1 to G3b, a known CKD-EPI creatinine–cystatin C stage, and a non-missing baseline creatinine eGFR. G4 and G5 are not matched; there are too few.
  2. Groups — reclassified worse by Cr-Cys is the treated group, same or better by Cr-Cys the control pool, exactly as in Section PREV15.
  3. Matching variable — baseline creatinine eGFR (eGFR_CRE_baseline), the quantity the two groups differ on at day 0.
  4. Caliper — a control must be within 2 mL/min/1.73m² of the treated patient’s baseline creatinine eGFR.
  5. Exact stratum — the control must also be in the same baseline creatinine CKD stage, so no pair straddles a stage boundary.
  6. Ratio — 1:1, without replacement; each control is used at most once.
  7. Choice inside the caliper — nearest neighbour on baseline creatinine eGFR.
  8. Order — treated patients with the fewest eligible controls are matched first, which maximises the number of pairs formed.
  9. Unmatched patients are dropped, treated and control alike.
  10. Balance check — Section 15.2 gives the standardised mean difference before and after. |SMD| < 0.1 is the usual threshold for adequate balance.

The five windows, the carry-forward rule and the small-cell suppression at 11 are unchanged from Section PREV15.

What this fixes, and what it does not. Matching removes the baseline gap and leaves the exposure intact — baseline cystatin C stays far apart after matching, because reclassification is defined by cystatin C being high relative to creatinine. It does not balance comorbidity (Charlson stays higher in the reclassified-worse group), it does not repair the window attrition described in Section 14, and it discards every patient who cannot be paired. Read these plots beside Section 13 rather than in place of it: the mixed model keeps every patient and every value, and its random intercept already absorbs the baseline level matched on here.

  "SMD = standardised mean difference."))

15.7 Slope over days 0-360 against days 90-360 (Carboplatin, matched)

The matched gap in 15.5 opens almost entirely between baseline and day 90 and is then flat. Progressive decline would widen the gap steadily; a step that appears at once and plateaus is what differential regression to the mean looks like, since the matched controls were picked for an unusually low reading and part of that is transient.

This fits the same random-intercept, random-slope model twice on the matched cohort — over days 0–360, then over days 90–360 with the first step excluded. Slopes are mL/min/1.73m² per year; the difference is reclassified-worse minus same-or-better, so a negative value means the worse group falls faster. If the day-0 to 90 step is driving the result, the difference shrinks towards zero in the days 90–360 rows.

Code 
# Mixed model on the matched cohort over a chosen day range. from_day = 0 keeps
# the baseline anchor as day 0; from_day = 90 drops it and every value before
# day 90, so the fit sees only the post-step part of the trajectory.
.match_slope <- function(d, from_day) {
  pat <- .match_bl(d) %>%
    dplyr::select(EMPI, ckd_shift2, eGFR_CRE_baseline) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ckd_shift2), !is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline))
  post <- pat %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(lmm_traj_all %>% dplyr::select(EMPI, cre_day, eGFR_CRE),
                      by = "EMPI") %>%
    filter(cre_day >= from_day, cre_day <= 360)
  lf <- if (from_day == 0)
          dplyr::bind_rows(
            pat %>% mutate(cre_day = 0, eGFR_CRE = eGFR_CRE_baseline), post)
        else post
  lf <- lf %>% mutate(time_yr = cre_day / 365) %>% droplevels()
  lmerTest::lmer(eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ckd_shift2 + (1 + time_yr | EMPI),
                 data = lf, control = LMM_CTL)
}

# One row: each group's annual slope, their difference, and the Satterthwaite
# test on the interaction.
.slope_row <- function(d, from_day, lbl) {
  fit <- .match_slope(d, from_day)
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients; nm <- names(b)
  it <- grep("^time_yr:ckd_shift2", nm, value = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(it)) return(NULL)
  est <- cf[it, "Estimate"]; se <- cf[it, "Std. Error"]
  tibble::tibble(
    Cohort = lbl,
    Days = if (from_day == 0) "0-360" else "90-360",
    Patients = as.integer(lme4::ngrps(fit)[["EMPI"]]),
    Values = as.integer(stats::nobs(fit)),
    `Same or better` = sprintf("%.1f", b[["time_yr"]]),
    `Reclassified worse` = sprintf("%.1f", b[["time_yr"]] + est),
    `Difference (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)",
                                    est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se),
    `p-value` = style_pvalue(cf[it, "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3))
}

.post90_table <- function() {
  surv <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    .slope_row(dat,  0,  "All patients"),
    .slope_row(dat,  90, "All patients"),
    .slope_row(surv, 0,  "Survivors"),
    .slope_row(surv, 90, "Survivors"))
}
.post90_table <- .wrap_tbl(.post90_table)

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(.post90_table()), caption = paste0(
  "Annual creatinine eGFR slope in the matched cohort, over days 0-360 and ",
  "over days 90-360. Difference is reclassified-worse minus same-or-better; ",
  "negative means the worse group falls faster."))
